And they took him away and buried him.
And he (or they?) set up in his place his son Ghiyath al-Din,
when he was about four years old.
In this year Nasir (or Radi?) al-Din Baba brought a command from the Ordo,
and he killed Zaki of Arbela,
and ruled in Mosul.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and seventy-eight
1578 of the Greeks [1267 AD],
King Hetoum came to Mosul,
and from there he went to the service of the King of Kings, Abaqa.
And he wept before him because of his son who was a prisoner in Egypt,
and he requested of him Sunqur al-Ashqar {OCR: Smqraya},
so that he might give him in exchange and receive back his son.
And he showed him favor and said to him:
"He is not near at hand now,
but you go to your country,
and I will bring him and send him to you."
And the king took leave and returned.
At this same time,
the Parwana,
the administrator of the realm of the Romans [Rûm], was filled with longing
to become related by marriage to King Hetoum through his daughter.
And he made an arrangement with Barsegh the Armenian monk, the king's envoy to the Tatars [Mongols].
And that foolish man advised him:
"When the king is prepared to pass through your territory, come to him and honor him,
and make your request of him,
and he will not refuse you."
Therefore, when the king returned from the Ordo,
and reached the inn (khan) of Karatay and spent the night there,
the Parwana came to him, and with him all the grandees of the Romans [Rûm],
and he offered the king very precious gifts,
and asked for his daughter.
And the king, because he was afraid
lest he should set an ambush for him on the road and harm him,
did not refuse him,
but gave him his word and his right hand,
and entered his own country.
And when the Parwana began to demand her,
the king replied
that it was not seemly to celebrate her wedding
while her brother was in captivity.
And when the Parwana had waited patiently until her brother arrived,
and no further excuse for delay remained,
it happened that the girl died;
and Barsegh the monk also perished in indignation.
And in the summer of this year, one thousand five hundred and seventy-eight (1578), Alam al-Riyasah, the Egyptian physician {OCR: nomikos}, was arrested in Mosul,
and was put to death in prison
on Monday the twenty-sixth
of Elul [September].
And in the year one thousand five hundred and seventy-nine (1579)
of the Greeks [1268 AD], Sunqur al-Ashqar was brought from the region of Samarkand,
and was sent to King Hetoum,
and he sent him to Egypt.
